A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ROC-based analysis of rejection sampling and Best-of-N. Their main text, mathematical statements, proofs, figures, notation table, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original Qwen and Llama experiments on GSM8K and MATH500 in Section 6 and Appendix F, including empirical scaling curves and aggregate accuracies.

after.justification: V3 retains original per-query experiments and reports revised aggregate comparisons, additional diagnostics, and GPQA and HumanEval+ results in Section 6 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: V2 uses constant-threshold RS and returns an incorrect null output after 25 unsuccessful samples in aggregate experiments. V3 introduces difficulty-dependent thresholds, using t or t/2 according to a 1% base-accuracy cutoff, and Capped RS, which returns the highest-scoring sampled answer when the cap is reached. These change acceptance and output procedures.

E1.justification: V3 retains GSM8K and MATH500 and adds GPQA STEM multiple-choice reasoning and HumanEval+ code generation (Figures E.7–E.8). This substantially broadens evaluation beyond mathematical question answering.

E2.justification: BoN remains the comparison method for RS, and matched experiments retain the existing Qwen3 and Llama verifier comparisons. The new RS variants extend the studied method; newly cited alternative approaches are not empirically benchmarked.

E3.justification: The main aggregate evaluation changes from constant thresholds and a null output after 25 failures to accuracy-dependent threshold groups and capped sampling with a fallback. New protocols include HumanEval+ comparisons at caps of 10 and 25, and a threshold-1 runtime diagnostic capped at 10,000 generations. These materially change the evaluated conditions.

E4.justification: V3 adds a focused diagnostic of extreme RS runtimes across queries (Figure E.1) and a HumanEval+ sensitivity comparison between sample caps of 25 and 10 (Figure E.8). Existing per-query ROC and scaling case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix E newly discloses a seed issue: aggregate experiments resample few-shot examples once per question, whereas individual GSM8K experiments resample them per generation. This adds seed information without establishing additional runs or a correction of the issue. Exact 90% confidence intervals remain the reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 Figure 5 is replaced by aggregate results for different RS procedures in v3 Figures 5a–b, so these are not performance gains under unchanged conditions. V3 adds GPQA and HumanEval+ results, including occasions where BoN beats RS capped at 25 on HumanEval+, while the cap of 10 appears more favorable. Figure E.1 reports 16 queries failing to reach threshold 1 within 10,000 generations. Retained per-query curves are unchanged.

T1.justification: V3 replaces Assumption 1 and the separate discrete-score smoothing treatment with randomized threshold definitions and a distributional-transform proof (Sections 3 and D.6). It generalizes Proposition 4 to measurable sets, adds the token-cost derivation using Wald's theorem, restricts Theorem 2 to finitely many linear pieces, and requires 0 < c < 1 in Proposition 7. Corrections throughout Appendix D revise extrapolation constructions, convex decomposition, and convergence arguments.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction explicitly condition RS dominance on a query having a concave verifier ROC curve, replacing unqualified wording or references to weak assumptions. The central ROC characterization, shared limiting accuracy, and impossibility of extrapolation remain. The discussion now treats hybrid methods as implemented approaches needing further refinement.

C2.justification: V3 substantially expands applicability qualifications: a common threshold can spend excessive compute on hard queries, while difficulty-dependent thresholds require information unavailable in practice. Section 6 motivates capped hybrids as a remedy. Appendix E qualifies empirical superiority through overlapping uncertainty and dependence on the sample cap, and explains how the seed issue could affect response diversity.

D1.justification: V3 adds GPQA and HumanEval+ generator prompts, a code-specific verifier prompt, and correctness-evaluation details using letter matching and EvalPlus (Appendices E–F). Existing temperature, few-shot count, MATH500 token cap, and GSM8K prompt code are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion of Chen et al. on compound AI systems and provable scaling, and Stroebl et al. on imperfect verifiers. Appendix B adds Wu et al. on reasoning length. New mathematical and benchmark references accompany the revision, while Rafailov et al. and Lan are removed. The central positioning around exact ROC characterization remains.

P1.justification: Most narrative and the main section order are retained. V3 makes terminology and copy edits, expands the aggregate-experiment explanation, subdivides Appendix C, and integrates the former standalone discrete-score discussion into the formal setup and proofs. Empirical and prompt appendices are consequently relabeled.

P2.justification: The aggregate-results presentation is substantially expanded: Figure 5 becomes separate rows for variable-threshold and capped RS, with Bo25 reference lines replacing maximum-RS lines. Three new appendix figures display runtime diagnostics and GPQA/HumanEval+ comparisons. Original Figures F.1–F.5 reappear as E.2–E.6, with empirical-versus-predicted caption corrections in the first four.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens the paper's mathematical reliability by unifying tied-score treatment and repairing important proof gaps, including the unjustified global Lipschitz argument in v2 Appendix D.11. It also addresses the aggregate sampling problem with tested alternatives and validation beyond mathematics. Explicit concavity conditions and new failure analyses better delimit the conclusions. Unknown query difficulty, overlapping confidence intervals, and the disclosed seed issue still limit empirical interpretation, but the gains in rigor and practical understanding support a substantial overall improvement.
